samples.summary: Mobile slides toolbar's `showRemoveLink` opt-in has no test, though the same argument the new test file makes for the desktop section applies
samples.evidence: `remove-link-button.test.ts` explicitly justifies asserting the opt-in at the call site ("the prop is optional, so a `showRemoveLink` that was never passed (or misspelled) fails silently — no type error") and does so only for `TextEditSection`. The identical opt-in added at `mobile-toolbar.tsx:580` has no coverage: the only `[aria-label="Remove link"]` query in packages/frontend/tests is in remove-link-button.test.ts, and `mobile-text-toggles.test.ts` only stubs `removeLink` on the fake editor without asserting the button renders. On mobile Slides, a dropped prop would leave no way to remove a hyperlink at all (Clear formatting now preserves them).

samples.summary: Newly extracted/behaviour-changed `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` has no direct unit test; its split-run guard and the `getBlock`→`findBlock` widening are untested
samples.evidence: grep for `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` finds it only in the three view files and its own module — no test file references it, and there is no `packages/docs/test/model/caret-style-trailing-edge`-style test (only `caret-style-surface.test.ts` exists). Two behaviours added/changed here are unexercised: (a) the `next.style.href === inline.style.href` continuation guard (no test builds a link split across two adjacent runs, e.g. a bold sub-run of the same URL), and (b) the switch from `getBlock` (threw → false) to `findBlock`, which newly makes the trailing-edge link exit fire for carets in headers, footers and table cells — no test places a caret at a link's trailing edge inside a table cell or header. A regression in either would silently extend or fail to exit a hyperlink.

samples.summary: The `prev.href === undefined` carry-over disjunct in all three new guards is never exercised by a test
samples.evidence: `pendingStyleFor` (editor.ts:1194-1196), `setPendingStyleGuarded` (text-editor.ts:3467-3469) and the text-box step (text-box-editor.ts:896-898) each OR `isAtLinkTrailingEdge(...)` with a check on the previously-armed pending `href: undefined`. Every new test (`Cmd+\ at a link trailing edge…`, `a toolbar toggle at a link trailing edge…`, `Cmd+B at a link trailing edge…`, the font-size cases) sets up a caret where `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` is already true, so the first disjunct short-circuits and the carry-over branch is dead as far as the suite is concerned. If it were deleted or inverted, no test would fail.
searchedFor: read all new tests in link-trailing-edge.test.ts

samples.summary: `pendingStyleFor`'s `if ('href' in style) return seed` escape hatch is untested
samples.evidence: No test calls `editor.applyStyle({ href: ... })` (or any collapsed-caret style write naming `href`) at a link trailing edge to prove the caller's explicit href wins over the guard. Searched packages/docs/test/view/link-trailing-edge.test.ts, editor-clear-formatting.test.ts and text-box-clear-formatting.test.ts; the only href-bearing writes go through `insertLink`/`removeLink`, which bypass `pendingStyleFor`. Removing that early return would not fail any test even though it would break a deliberate link-setting write.

samples.summary: text-box `removeLink`'s partial-selection semantics ("unlinks exactly what it covers") is not tested
samples.evidence: The two new selection tests cover only the extremes: `removeLink drops a link the selection covers…` (select-all) and `removeLink leaves a link the selection does not touch` (selection over 'now'). Neither exercises a selection that partially overlaps a link, which is the case the implementation comment explicitly reasons about (text-box-editor.ts:1264-1267). Additionally, the 'does not touch' test would pass unchanged against the old caret-only implementation, so it cannot distinguish the new branch.

samples.summary: The Cmd+\ drift fix is only asserted for `color`; `fontSize`, `fontFamily` and `backgroundColor` — three of the four keys the shortcut used to omit — are not in the fixture
samples.evidence: `clearFormatting` was changed to use `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`, whose stated purpose (text-editor.ts:3420-3424) is that the shortcut had omitted `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `color` and `backgroundColor`. The new test 'the Mod+\ shortcut keeps the hyperlink too' only asserts `link?.style.color` is falsy, and `linkedBlock` (line 127) sets none of fontSize/fontFamily/backgroundColor. A regression that re-omitted those three keys from the shortcut path would not be caught.

samples.summary: 'a collapsed-caret clear at a link trailing edge keeps the link intact' asserts a call that is a no-op by construction, duplicating existing space-exit coverage
samples.evidence: The test's own comment concedes the call stages nothing: `clearInlineFormatting` → `applyStyleImpl` returns immediately without a selection (text-box-editor.ts:824). What the assertions actually verify — that typing a space after a link exits the link — is already covered verbatim by `text-box-link-trailing-edge.test.ts:116` ('typing a space right after an inserted link does not extend the link'). It provides near-zero incremental signal about the clear-formatting change.

samples.summary: 'keeps the href while clearing the formatting on the same run' passes vacuously if the synthetic select-all keydown does not take effect
samples.evidence: The test relies on a dispatched Ctrl/Meta+'a' keydown to build the selection; both `applyStyle` and `clearInlineFormatting` no-op without one (text-box-editor.ts:824). If the selection were not established, `bold`/`color` would never be applied, so `expect(inline.style.bold).toBeFalsy()`, `color` falsy and `href` preserved would all hold regardless of the change under test. `TextEditor.selectAll` (text-editor.ts:3395) does run for `mod && key === 'a'` and jsdom's non-Mac platform makes `mod = ctrlKey`, so it most likely works — but the test never asserts that the selection or the intermediate bold/colour write actually took, which is what would make it non-vacuous by construction.
